messages:
chris_support: Anyone seeing SSE streams get elided on reconnects? Customer report: final JSON object truncated, no finish_reason, and client-side parse fails.

chris_support: Repro steps I followed:
```bash
# server: start stream
curl -N -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/stream \ 
  -d '{"model":"xsmall","prompt":"long output"}'
# quickly kill client (ctrl-c) then reconnect with resume header
curl -N -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -H 'X-Resume-From: 0-12345' https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/stream
```

chris_support: First response shows truncated tail (notice trailing comma + no final event):
```json
{"choices":[{"delta":{"content":"..."}},],
```
(no \n\n and no finish_reason)

maria_sys: Thanks. Can you paste the request_id and proxy path? Also which customer region (us-west / eu)?

chris_support: request_id=rid_03b7d, customer region: us-west-2. Path went through edge > fastly > internal gateway. Fastly logs show:
```
Fastly: connection timed out, keepalive flush after 30s
gateway: upstream closed socket while streaming
runtime: stream flushed without terminal event
```

sam_engineer: Two likely causes: (1) edge/proxy kills connection mid-emit (fastly/timeout/keepalive) and our runtime fails to emit the final SSE event before socket close, (2) resume header handling ignores last buffered tail so reconnect resumes earlier chunk and the last partial object is never sent.

sam_engineer: Quick check: does the client set Last-Event-ID or X-Resume-From correctly? If the server uses byte-range style resume the offsets must line up. Mismatched resume offset will skip the final chunk.

kelly_oncall: Immediate customer workaround: treat SSE as eventually-consistent — retry on parse failure by re-requesting the last N tokens non-streaming. Also, tolerant parse: if stream ends with a trailing comma or incomplete object, attempt to append closing brace and reparse, then fetch missing tokens from non-stream endpoint.

chris_support: I tried ledgering last_event_id but the client library (browser code) only uses reconnect without header. The second reconnect POST contained different cookies so gateway treated it as a new session and our resume code path was skipped.

maria_sys: Can you attach the server runtime logs around rid_03b7d (±60s)? Also include the exact curl reproducer output (raw bytes). I'll pull fastly traces.

chris_support: Pasted snippets above and uploaded full logs to the support ticket. Reproducer raw shows the server emitted the final "}\n\n" on stdout but the connection saw FIN right after; fastly sent a TCP FIN before the final packet reached client. We also see our runtime earlier emitting a keepalive heartbeat event every 15s.

sam_engineer: That heartbeat is suspicious — on reconnect we may emit a heartbeat with an event id that gets GC'd then the resumed stream drops the final content due to race. Two short-term fixes: (A) ensure runtime always sends terminal event before any connection-close sequence (explicit flush + final sentinel), (B) change heartbeat interval to longer than proxy idle timeout or disable heartbeats when connection is proxied through fastly.

kelly_oncall: Ops note: we rolled a Fastly VCL change last week to aggressively close idle connections after 28s to reduce origin costs. That could have clipped tails for long-running streams. @maria_sys can you confirm which deployments saw the VCL? If so, we should revert/raise timeout and queue a canary.

deploy-bot: deploy notif: rollout fastly-vcl-2026-03-15 completed to prod-us-west-2 at 2026-03-15T12:05:02Z (rollout id: roll_7789)

maria_sys: Confirmed — prod-us-west-2 got fastly-vcl-2026-03-15. That matches timings. Next steps: 1) short-term: recommend customer to use non-stream endpoint or implement tolerant-reconnect; 2) ops: revert/patch VCL to 60s for streams; 3) eng-runtime: patch to always emit explicit terminal SSE event and to atomically flush it before closing socket.

sam_engineer: I'll open an ENG ticket to change runtime behavior (force final \n\n sentinel, atomic flush). Also adding better resume semantics: server must accept last_event_id and re-send any bytes after that offset, not just start-from-chunk-id.

chris_support: Logged support ticket SUP-2026-109 with attachments + minimal repro script and timeline. Customer is on a paid Dedicated plan and this is impacting queued API calls (billing note: they were billed for tokens but didn't receive final tokens). Need priority handling.

maria_sys: Ops will revert VCL for streams in us-west-2 to 60s now. eng: please triage kinetic fix. Thanks everyone :thumbsup
notes: thread contains logs, curl repro, and action items: revert fastly VCL, runtime patch to always flush terminal event, client tolerant parsing and resume header fixes
